title: Coding Standard (React)
description: Conventions and habits for readable, maintainable React and TypeScript — stack defaults, validation, naming, and error handling.

blocks.content: Coding rules and guidelines that keep software **safe**, **secure**, **reliable**, **testable**, **maintainable**, and **portable** — especially useful when multiple engineers share a React codebase.

blocks.body: Treat this as practices and conventions, not a rigid lint config. Prefer the project's existing stack when it already has a clear alternative.

items.label: 2. Turn daily backups into an instinct

blocks.content: Coding rules and guidelines that ensure that software is:

items: **Safe** — it can be used with minimal harm
**Secure** — it should be as un-hackable as we can make it
**Reliable** — it functions as it should, every time
**Testable** — it can be tested at the code level
**Maintainable** — it can be maintained, even as your codebase grows
**Portable** — it works the same in every environment

blocks.content: Even the most experienced developer could unintentionally introduce a coding defect. And that one defect could lead to a minor glitch — or worse, a serious security breach.

items: Offers uniformity to the codes created by different engineers
Enables the creation of reusable codes
Makes it easier to detect errors
Makes codes simpler, more readable, and easier to maintain
Boost programming efficiency and generate faster results

blocks.content: A typical modern React setup. Swap pieces when the project already has a clear alternative (e.g. Vitest instead of Jest).

items: **React** — UI library: components, hooks, and rendering
**TypeScript** — static types for props, state, and APIs; catches many mistakes before runtime
**Vite or Next.js** — app shell and tooling. Vite for SPAs/client apps; Next.js when you want routing, SSR/SSG, and file-based pages
**TanStack Query (React Query)** — server/async state: fetching, caching, retries, and background refetch for APIs
**Zod** — runtime schema validation for forms, env, and API payloads (pairs well with TypeScript)

**Vitest or Jest + React Testing Library** — unit/component tests. Vitest is the common default with Vite; Jest remains fine in many codebases. RTL exercises components the way users interact with them
**ESLint** — lint rules for React/TS consistency and common bugs; often paired with Prettier for formatting

blocks.content: Prefer **clear over clever**. Someone else (or future you) should understand the code without a guided tour.

items: Use meaningful names for variables, functions, files, and directories — spelling matters for searchability
Keep functions short and focused: one function, one job
Prefer DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself), but do not abstract so early that the code becomes harder to follow
Avoid deep nesting; early returns and small helpers flatten control flow
Prefer shorter lines and logical blank lines between related blocks so structure is obvious at a glance
Let formatting tools (Prettier/ESLint) handle indentation and spacing consistently
Avoid long lines — it is easier for humans to read blocks that are horizontally short and vertically long
Avoid spelling mistakes in variables, files, and directory names for better readability and searchability

blocks.content: 2. Turn daily backups into an instinct

items: Multiple events can trigger data loss: system crash, dead battery, software glitch, hardware damage, etc.
To prevent this, save code daily, and after every modification, no matter how minuscule it may be
Push your codes to github daily

blocks.content: Do not assume that just because everyone else viewing the code is a developer, they will instinctively understand it without clarification. Devs are human, and it is a lot easier for them to read comments describing code function rather than scanning the code and making speculations.

Take an extra minute to write a comment describing the code function at various points in the script. Ensure that the comments guide any readers through the algorithm and logic implemented. Of course, this is only required when the code's purpose is not apparent.
Remove unnecessarily commented codes to keep the codebase clean.

blocks.body: **Do not bother leaving comments on self-explanatory code.**

blocks.content: Failures will happen (network errors, bad API payloads, unexpected nulls). Handle them so the app stays usable and the problem is diagnosable — do not let them fail silently or crash the whole tree when a local fallback will do.

items: **Catch at the right layer.** Use `try/catch` (or `.catch`) around async work you own: `fetch`, parsers, storage. Prefer handling errors in data/hooks layers and returning a clear result to the UI, instead of scattering catch blocks in every component.
**Do not swallow errors.** An empty `catch` hides bugs. Log with context (what failed, relevant ids), then surface a user-facing message or rethrow when the caller should decide.
**Be specific.** Prefer typed/narrow failures (`if (!res.ok) throw new Error(`Load user failed: ${res.status}`)`) over a generic "something went wrong" with no detail for logs.
**Separate UI crash from data failure.** Render-time React errors need an **Error Boundary** (fallback UI for that subtree). Failed fetches belong in query/`useEffect` error state, not in a boundary.
**Show recovery in the UI.** Offer retry, go back, or a safe empty state. With TanStack Query, use `isError` / `error` and a Retry action rather than leaving a blank screen.
**Validate external input.** Treat API and form data as untrusted; validate with something like Zod so bad shapes become expected errors, not random runtime crashes.

blocks.content: All user-facing input fields should be validated, at least on the frontend, before submit or side effects. Prefer a schema library (e.g. Zod) so rules stay in one place; still show clear field-level messages in the UI.

items: **Required fields:** if a value is not optional, reject `null`, `undefined`, and empty strings (trim whitespace before checking).
**Types and formats:** emails, phones, dates, and IDs should match the expected shape — not just "non-empty."
**Numbers and currency:** parse as numbers; reject NaN; for money, limit decimal places (often 2) and disallow negative amounts unless the domain allows it.
**Ranges and length:** min/max for numbers, string length, and list size where the product cares.
**Surface errors early:** disable or block submit while invalid, and show which field failed — do not only fail after the API round-trip.
Variable names should be meaningful
`firstName` should be preferred over `fN`
Do not use a single identifier for multiple purposes
Ascribe a name to each variable that clearly describes its purpose
Single variables cannot be assigned multiple values or used for numerous functions
Always assign unique variable or argument names

blocks.content: Use `const` variables for repeated strings to reduce the risk of spelling mistakes.
Use a variable or helper method for complicated expressions. If there are too many `&&` or `||` in a condition and/or the condition is repeated multiple times, assign it to a variable.
If it requires more calculation with context, convert it to a helper method.

blocks.content: Prefer destructuring for cleaner React/TypeScript code — props, nested state, and API payloads.

blocks.code:
const city = formState.address.city;
const country = formState.address.country;
const { city, country } = formState.address;

const name = data.user.profile.name;
const email = data.user.profile.email;
const { name, email } = data.user.profile;

items: File and directory names should be meaningful
Component names should be in PascalCase — `ComponentOne.tsx`, `Header.tsx`, `NewsArticle.tsx`
Non-component names should be in camelCase — `useMyCustomHook.ts`, `fetchApi.ts`, `myUtilityFile.ts`
Unit tests should use the same names as their corresponding file — `ComponentOne.tsx` / `ComponentOne.test.tsx`
Attributes/props should be camelCase — `className`, `onClick`, `someCustomAttribute`
Use this pattern: `{project}-{module}-{component}-{part}`
**Wrapper** contains parts that make up one component
**Container** contains different components and wrappers

blocks.body: This layout is a **starting recommendation**, not a permanent law. It may change as the starter and team conventions evolve. Prefer whatever the live repo documents when they diverge from this article.

blocks.content: The reference shape comes from the [starter-mfe](https://github.com/ikikika/learning/tree/react/starter-mfe/react/starter-mfe) branch — a Webpack Module Federation React starter (`standalone` | `host` | `remote` | `hybrid`). Use it as the default mental model for where code belongs.

blocks.code:
starter-mfe/
  src/
    app/           # wiring: providers, routes, federated entries, remote loaders
    features/      # domain UI + api / hooks / types per feature
    pages/         # thin route containers that compose features
    components/    # shared UI primitives (not domain logic)
    core/          # shared constants, role/remotes helpers, shared hooks
    services/      # shared HTTP client (httpClient, apiUrl)
    layouts/       # shell chrome (e.g. MainLayout)
    styles/        # tokens + global styles
    types/         # shared TypeScript types
  tests/           # contract + integration (unit tests stay co-located)
  config/          # build / tooling config
  docs/            # conventions, overview, UI context
  public/          # static assets, PWA manifest
  scripts/         # init, add-remote, env helpers
  specs/           # Speckit feature specs (optional)

sections.title: Layer terms
sections.body:
* **Feature** — a vertical slice of product behavior (`src/features/<name>/`). Owns its UI, API functions, hooks, and local types. Example: `auth`, `demoHost`, `demoRemote`.
* **Page** — a thin route container under `src/pages/`. Composes features and layouts; should not grow into heavy domain logic or raw `fetch` calls.
* **App wiring** — `src/app/`: root `App.tsx`, role route tables (`standaloneRoutes`, `hostRoutes`, …), providers, and Module Federation mounts (`FederatedRemoteApp`, `FederatedHybridApp`, remote loaders).
* **Component (shared)** — reusable presentational primitives in `src/components/` (Button, ThemeToggle). No feature-specific API knowledge.
* **Core** — cross-app constants and helpers: `apiRoutes`, `routePaths`, role/remotes metadata. Path strings and env-derived values live here, not hardcoded in UI.
* **Service** — shared HTTP plumbing in `src/services/` (`httpClient`, `apiUrl`). Feature `api/` modules call through this layer.
* **Layout** — chrome around pages (nav, header band) in `src/layouts/`.
* **MFE role** — how this clone runs under Module Federation: **standalone** (single app), **host** (shell that loads remotes), **remote** (leaf exposed to a host), **hybrid** (intermediate shell that both exposes itself and loads child remotes).

sections.title: App folder shape
sections.body:
```text
src/app/
  App.tsx                    # own-app root (providers + role routes)
  FederatedRemoteApp.tsx     # public MF expose for remote role
  FederatedHybridApp.tsx     # public MF expose for hybrid role
  providers/                 # ThemeProvider, AppProviders, PWA register
  routes/                    # role route tables (standalone / host / remote / hybrid)
  remotes/                   # LoadRemote, per-alias loaders (host / hybrid)
```

* `App.tsx` is for running this package as its own app — providers and PWA apply here, not via the federated expose.
* Role route files map URLs to thin pages; path segments come from `routePaths` in `src/core/constants/`.
* Host/hybrid remotes: `loaders.generated.ts` is produced by init / `add-remote`; mount slots with `<LoadRemote alias="…" />`.

sections.title: Feature folder shape
sections.body:
```text
src/features/<name>/
  api/           # pure HTTP / data-access functions (e.g. getPost.ts)
  hooks/         # React hooks: loading / success / error (+ abort)
  types/         # feature-local request/response / view types
  <Name>.tsx     # presentational UI (consume hooks/props only)
  <Name>.module.scss
  <Name>.test.tsx
  index.ts       # public exports (especially for federated exposes)
```

Preferred create order: **types → api → hooks → presentational UI → page/route wiring**.

sections.title: Where to put common work
sections.body:
* **New product capability / screen flow** → `src/features/<name>/` (types, api, hooks, UI), then a thin page under `src/pages/`, then wire the path in the matching `src/app/routes/*Routes.tsx` using `routePaths` from `src/core/constants/`.
* **Shared button, toggle, fallback UI** → `src/components/<Name>/` (no feature API imports).
* **Shell nav / page chrome** → `src/layouts/`.
* **API path segments / URL helpers** → `src/core/constants/apiRoutes.ts` (then `apiUrl()` from `services`).
* **App route path segments** → `src/core/constants/routePaths.ts` — do not hardcode compose/leaf paths in components or route tables.
* **HTTP client / base URL wiring** → `src/services/httpClient.ts`; base URL from env via `src/core/constants/app.ts`.
* **Theme tokens / global CSS** → `src/styles/tokens.css` and `global.scss`; co-locate component styles as `*.module.scss`.
* **Unit tests** → co-located next to the source (`*.test.tsx`). **Contract / integration** → `tests/`.
* **Federated remote/hybrid entry** → expose from `src/app/FederatedRemoteApp.tsx` / `FederatedHybridApp.tsx`; keep domain UI in features; pass `embedded={true}` when a host mounts you.
* **Host remote slot / loader** → `src/app/remotes/` + remotes metadata in `src/core/constants/remotes.ts` (and `npm run add-remote` for host/hybrid clones).

blocks.body: Layer rule of thumb: **pages compose, features own domain data, components stay presentational, core holds shared constants, services own HTTP.** Do not call APIs from presentational components (including via `useEffect` in the component body) — put that in `features/*/hooks` + `features/*/api`.

A condensed, agent-ready version of these practices lives in [REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md](/REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md) — download that file and add it to any React project so coding agents follow the same conventions.
To wire it into a project via `AGENTS.md` (a common, tool-agnostic entry point many agents read automatically):

items: Download [REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md](/REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md)
Copy it into the project root (keep the filename, or place it under something like `docs/REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md`)
Create or open `AGENTS.md` at the project root
Add a short pointer so agents load it (example below)
Commit both files so every agent and teammate picks up the same instructions

blocks.code:
## React coding practices

Follow [REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md](./REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md) for React/TypeScript conventions. Prefer existing project patterns when they conflict with that file.

blocks.body: If your agent does not auto-read `AGENTS.md`, paste the contents of `REACT_CODING_PRACTICES.md` into that tool’s custom instructions, or @-mention / attach the file in the chat.
